A_target.statement:
Let $f: \closedint a b \to \closedint a b$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]].
Then there exists $c \in \closedint a b$ with $\map f c = c$.

B_source.statement:
Let $g$ be continuous on $\closedint a b$ and let $k$ lie between $\map g a$ and $\map g b$.
Then there exists $c \in \closedint a b$ with $\map g c = k$.

object_map.reformulation: Encode the fixed point equation f(x) = x as a root of the displacement f(x) - x.

validity_conditions: f must map the interval into itself, which gives the endpoint signs of the displacement.
The argument is special to dimension 1, where intervals are the only connected sets.
proof_plan: Let $\map g x = \map f x - x$, which is continuous on $\closedint a b$.

As $\map f a \ge a$ and $\map f b \le b$:
:$\map g a \ge 0 \ge \map g b$
By the [[Intermediate Value Theorem]], there is $c$ with $\map g c = 0$.
